content: Leanne Jones is affiliated with the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group at the University of Liverpool in Liverpool, United Kingdom. Theresa Lawrie serves as the Director of The Evidence-Based Medicine Consultancy Ltd, located in Bath, United Kingdom. Myfanwy Williams is also associated with the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group at the University of Liverpool in Liverpool, United Kingdom. Rodolfo Gomez Ponce de Leon is a Reproductive Health Advisor at the Latin American Center for Perinatology, Women, and Reproductive Health (CLAP/WR) in Montevideo, Uruguay. Tamar Kabakian is an Associate Professor in Health Promotion and Community Health at the Faculty of Health Sciences, American University of Beirut, Lebanon. Petr Velebil is an Obstetrician at the Perinatal Centre of the Institute for the Care of Mother and Child in Prague, Czech Republic. Yacouba Yaro is the Director General of the Center for Studies, Research, and Training for Economic and Social Development (CERFODES) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Dr. Niveen Abu-Rmeileh specializes in community and public health as well as statistical epidemiology. She declared no conflicts of interest. Dr. Luz Maria De-Regil has expertise in nutrition, epidemiology, systematic reviews, and program implementation. She authored publications on multiple micronutrient supplements for pregnant women and vitamin D supplementation. She was previously employed by Nutrition International, a non-profit organization delivering micronutrient interventions, but this was not deemed a significant conflict of interest. Dr. Atf Ghérissi focuses on systematic reviews, qualitative evidence, maternal and perinatal health, and community health, with no declared conflicts of interest. Ms. Gill Gyte, a consumer representative in pregnancy and childbirth, declared no conflicts of interest. Dr. Rintaro Mori specializes in perinatology, neonatology, systematic reviews, evidence synthesis, and guideline development using GRADE methodology, with no declared conflicts of interest. Prof. Jim Neilson, an expert in general obstetrics, perinatology, gynecology, systematic reviews, and evidence synthesis, also declared no conflicts of interest. Dr. Lynnette Neufeld has expertise in micronutrients, programs, and epidemiology. She declared no conflicts of interest, and her involvement in technical consultations was not affected. Prof. Nafissa Osman specializes in obstetrics and gynecology as well as implementation research, with no declared conflicts of interest. Dr. Erika Ota focuses on nutrition, evidence synthesis, and guideline development, with no declared conflicts of interest. Prof. Robert Pattinson is an expert in obstetrics and gynecology, delivery of care, and evidence synthesis, with no declared conflicts of interest. Prof. Harshi Sachdev, specializing in pediatrics, nutrition, and systematic reviews, contributed data from India to meta-analyses and co-authored a paper on multiple micronutrients in pregnancy. This was not considered a significant conflict of interest. Ms. Rusidah Selamat focuses on maternal and infant nutrition, community-based programs, and implementation research, with no declared conflicts of interest. Dr. Charlotte Warren specializes in maternal and perinatal health, systematic reviews, and implementation research, with no declared conflicts of interest. Prof. Charles Wiysonge is an expert in health systems, systematic reviews, and delivery of care, with no declared conflicts of interest. The GRADE tables and forest plots for antenatal vitamin D supplementation compare the effects of vitamin D alone versus placebo or no intervention during pregnancy. Studies were conducted in various countries, including Australia, Bangladesh, Brazil, China, France, India, Iran, New Zealand, Pakistan, Russia, and the United Kingdom. However, most outcome data were derived from studies in India and Iran. The analysis highlights potential biases, regional differences in skin pigmentation and clothing affecting sunlight exposure, and the inclusion of high-risk populations for conditions like eclampsia and gestational diabetes mellitus. The evidence quality was rated as very low due to imprecision, few events, and potential publication bias. Similarly, the effects of vitamin D plus calcium supplementation versus no supplementation were analyzed, with most data derived from studies in India and Iran. The evidence quality was also rated as very low, with explanations including imprecision, few events, and potential biases in the pooled data.
